subject: Go/No-Go Review: hosting path readiness & security evidence for Cortex Health
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cortexhealth.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@cortexhealth.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Go/No-Go Review: hosting path readiness & security evidence for Cortex Health

Hi Jordan / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get to a go/no‑go decision with Procurement and InfoSec by the end of next week.

Call recap (30m):
- Primary constraint: Cortex will process PHI for lab results and imaging metadata; legal needs a signed BAA and InfoSec team needs SOC2 evidence.
- Preferred residency: US-only right now, potential APAC later.
- Main question for us: whether Cortex needs Private (VPC/on‑prem) or whether Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in our environment) + BAA will be acceptable.

Redwood options (brief):
1) Hosted API: fastest to production, but does not satisfy Cortex's requirement for a customer‑managed network boundary. Not recommended for PHI.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation; can be combined with a BAA and custom routing; good middle ground if Cortex accepts our isolation controls.
3) Private (VPC / on‑prem): full control for Cortex — recommended if Procurement or legal mandates network ownership or on‑prem hosting.

What we need from Cortex (asks):
- Confirm whether Procurement will accept a BAA + Dedicated capacity, or if they require Private/VPC/on‑prem. A simple yes/no here will let us prioritize the technical plan.
- Provide the primary security contact (name + email) who will own the SOC2/BAA review.
- If you have a standard security questionnaire, please share — we can fill and return within 48 hours.
- Any constraints on audit windows (e.g., need for on‑site audits, 3rd‑party assessor access).
- Target go/no‑go date: you mentioned a procurement checkpoint on 6/21 — can we aim for a decision by EOD 6/21?

What Redwood will provide (by EOD tomorrow):
- Redacted SOC2 Type II report (most recent). Link/attachment below.
- Standard BAA template for review.
- High‑level network diagram and data flow (PHI classification + audit logging retention).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Jordan to confirm whether Procurement accepts BAA + Dedicated, or requires Private/VPC (reply to this thread).
2) If BAA is acceptable: we’ll share SOC2 redacted + BAA and schedule a 30m technical follow‑up with Monica for network design.
3) If Private required: schedule architecture workshop (Aditya and Monica) and provide preliminary estimate for onboarding timeline.

Attachments: we’ll send a redacted SOC2 and BAA template in the next message.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Sean — good summary. A few quick answers and a couple of clarifying asks from our side.

Answers: 
- Procurement stance: likely to accept a BAA + Dedicated capacity if we can show the SOC2 Type II report (last 12 months) and a network diagram that demonstrates tenant isolation and audit logging. If Procurement legal flags any ambiguity we may have to shift to Private/VPC, but that is a heavier procurement lift.
- Security contact: Jordan Lee (CTO) — jordan.lee@cortexhealth.ai (me). InfoSec reviewer: Alyssa Park (cc’d).
- Audit windows: we do expect the ability to attend a remote audit and to receive exported logs for a 24‑month retention period. On‑site assessor access is only required if a Private/on‑prem route is chosen.

Attached: cortex_security_qs.pdf — our baseline questionnaire (we filled sections already; marked a few areas pending). Please confirm whether you can provide the SOC2 redacted report and a BAA draft to share with our legal by EOD tomorrow.

If you can provide those artifacts, Procurement will aim to make a determination on 6/21. If we need Private, we’ll raise a procurement ticket this week.

Jordan / Alyssa —

Appreciate the quick reply and the questionnaire — that helps a lot. Putting Monica (me) as technical owner for the follow‑up network design and Aditya on commercial / procurement coordination. A few commitments from our side and suggested next steps: 

What Redwood will provide (by EOD tomorrow):
- redwood_soc2_type2_2027_redacted.pdf (redacted SOC2 Type II report) — attached.
- redwood_baa_template.docx (BAA draft) — attached.
- A one‑page network & dataflow diagram showing tenant isolation, KV cache boundaries, and audit log export points.
- Our audit logging retention policy: 24 months by default; exportable for customer audits on request.

Suggested small‑step path: Dedicated capacity + signed BAA
- Why: Dedicated gives isolation, predictable throughput, and we can enable additional network controls (private peering options) faster than a full Private/VPC/on‑prem engagement.
- If Procurement insists on Private, we’ll escalate a timeline and workshop; note Private typically adds 6–10 weeks to onboarding depending on networking approvals.

Action items / owners:
- Sean: send redacted SOC2 + BAA (done — attached).
- Jordan / Alyssa: confirm whether Procurement accepts Dedicated + BAA (reply to this thread).
- Monica (me): schedule a 30m technical follow‑up to walk through the one‑page network diagram — available 6/16 or 6/17.
- Aditya: prepare preliminary commercial estimate for Dedicated onboarding and runbook.

If we can confirm BAA acceptance by 6/21, we’ll treat that as a go and can begin account provisioning the following week. If not, we’ll treat as a Private path and schedule the architecture workshop.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
